text: synthetic case : a tea garden supervisor with continuous service for over 240 days in a calendar year was orally discharged without written notice, prior inquiry, or retrenchment compensation mandated under section 25f of the industrial disputes act. management alleged performance issues without holding a domestic inquiry. district court examined muster rolls and pay slips, holding the termination illegal and directing statutory relief. ruling : accepted.

synthetic case : group of rural workers deployed at a processing facility petitioned for 5 months of accrued unpaid wages. the employer claimed financial distress and crop yield loss justified delayed disbursements. high court affirmed that statutory minimum wage obligations under the payment of wages framework cannot be deferred or contingent on commercial profitability. ruling : rejected.

synthetic case : daily - wage workers engaged continuously for over 8 years against sanctioned public works vacancies sought absorption into regular cadre. state authorities argued the initial recruitment lacked formal selection process. supreme court evaluated unbroken service records and directed consideration for regularization under applicable public employment policies. ruling : partial.

synthetic case : a plantation laborer suffered severe partial disability due to an unshielded machine unit at a rural plant. management offered minor ex - gratia assistance while denying statutory liability under the employee's compensation act. district court evaluated medical disability certificates and loss of earning capacity, ordering full statutory compensation. ruling : accepted.

synthetic case : retired seasonal employee denied terminal gratuity benefits on grounds that seasonal employment interrupted continuous service requirements. high court held that seasonal engagements meeting statutory minimum operational days satisfy the threshold under the payment of gratuity act. ruling : rejected.

synthetic case : contractual female brick kiln loader was denied 26 weeks paid maternity leave and subsequently terminated upon applying for leave. employer relied on private contract terms excluding statutory maternity benefits. supreme court ruled that statutory entitlements under the maternity benefit act override private contractual restrictions. ruling : partial.

synthetic case : agricultural laborers demonstrated that cash wages paid by a commercial farm were lower than state - notified minimum wage rates, with unnotified deductions made for basic shelter. district court prohibited unnotified wage deductions and directed back - pay calculation based on official minimum wage notifications. ruling : accepted.

synthetic case : assembly line workers engaged via an intermediary labor contractor performed core operational tasks alongside permanent workers for half pay. high court found the contract labor arrangement to be a sham mechanism designed to evade equal pay mandates, directing parity in remuneration. ruling : rejected.

synthetic case : inter - state migrant laborers detained at a brick kiln due to alleged advance debt obligations filed for relief under the bonded labour system ( abolition ) act. supreme court directed immediate release, cancellation of alleged debts, and state rehabilitation assistance. ruling : partial.

synthetic case : factory workers required to work 12 - hour daily shifts without overtime payment petitioned under factories welfare rules. district court verified shift logbooks and ordered payment of double - rate statutory overtime wages. ruling : accepted.

synthetic case : industrial unit management instituted sudden site closure without serving 60 days prior statutory notice to the labor commissioner. high court declared the lockout illegal and awarded full wage continuity during the closure period. ruling : rejected.

synthetic case : union office - bearers were target - transferred to remote sites immediately following the submission of a collective bargaining charter. supreme court held the transfers to be unfair labor practice intended to suppress union activities and issued stay orders. ruling : partial.

synthetic case : trainees engaged under apprentice designations were deployed on core production machinery for over 3 years without formal training or stipend adjustment. district court recognized them as regular workmen entitled to statutory wage scales. ruling : accepted.
